s: Partition of Bengal was done mainly for :

To weaken the growth of Nationalism in Bengal
x: “The Partition of Bengal, said Lord Curzon, was a mere readjustment of administrative boundaries.” The argument advocated for the partition was that it would improve the administration of the two provinces. s: August 7 was chosen as the National Handloom Day to commemorate the ____.
What was the immediate cause for the launch of the Swadeshi Movement?
o: The partition of Bengal done by Lord Curzon.
A sentence of eighteen months rigorous imprisonment imposed on Lokmanya Tilak.
The arrest and deportation of Lala Lajpat Rai and Ajit Singh, and passing of the Punjab Colonisation Bill.
Death sentence pronounced on the Chapekar brothers.
x: The Swadeshi Movement was launched in 1905 as a direct response to the Partition of Bengal announced by Lord Curzon. The partition was perceived as a deliberate attempt to divide Bengal on communal lines and weaken the nationalist movement. The movement promoted self-reliance (Swadeshi) by boycotting foreign goods and using Indian products, uniting diverse groups in a nationwide movement for self-rule, and leading to a significant cultural and political awakening.

s: Which of the following movements is not related to Gandhiji?
x: Gandhiji was not related to the Swadeshi Movement. Swadeshi Movement was started to protest against the partition of Bengal in 1905 A.D. and continued up to 1911. During this period, Gandhi was residing in South Africa. The rest of the other movements were led by Mahatma Gandhi.

s: Which movement started after the Partition of Bengal?
x: 6. The Declaration of Partition of Bengal was done on -: (a) 19th July, 1905 (b) 7th August, 1905 (c) 15th August, 1905 (d) 16th October, 1905 (e) None of the above/More than one of the above 63rd B.P.S.C (Pre.) 2017 Ans (a) The decision to Partition of Bengal was announced on 20th July 1905 A.D. by British India government. However on 19th July 1905 A.D. the resolution of the declaration of partition of Bengal signed. Because of this BPSC had given (a) as correct option.

s: Who was the first to suggest the boycott of British goods in Bengal?
x: Krishna Kumar Mitra was an Indian freedom fighter, journalist, and leader of Brahmo Samaj. He was an active leader and was against the partition of Bengal. On 13 July, 1905 AD, In his Nationalist Bengali weekly Magazine titled ‘Sanjibani’ he boldly advocated for the freedom of the press. In his opinion, the manufacturing of British goods should be abolished. He called for a boycott of foreign goods, government officials and organisations by breaking all connections, people should mourn etc. His ideas were supported by a gathering in District Bagerhat (Division-Khulna) on 16 July, 1905 A.D.

s: Boycott of British goods was adopted as a national policy in –
x: Lord Curzon announced the partition of Bengal on July 20, 1905 A.D. As a result, Swadeshi Movement was announced in Townhall, Kolkata on August 7, 1905 A.D., and ‘Boycott Proposal’ was passed. The boycott of British goods was adopted as a national policy in this meeting.

s: Anti-partition Movement of Bengal was initiated on
x: The anti-partition (Swadeshi) movement was formally launched on 7 August 1905 with the boycott resolution at Calcutta Town Hall. 20 July was the partition announcement and 16 October the day it took effect.

Curzon’s attempt to control the Universities.
Curzon’s plan to curb the growing popularity of the Indian National Congress.
x: The partition of Bengal by Curzon was the immediate cause that spread Swadeshi and boycott. The other Curzon measures were not the direct trigger.

s: Which movement was started as a reaction to the Partition of Bengal?
x: The Swadeshi Movement arose as a reaction to the partition of Bengal. Non-Cooperation was not a programme against the partition.

s: With reference to the period of extremist nationalist movement in India with its spirit of Swadeshi, which one of the following statements is not correct?

x: of the villages The peasant agitations in Barisal were led by Ashwini Kumar Dutt, who exercised considerable influence in the region through the Swadesh Bandhab Samiti. Liaquat Hussain was a prominent nationalist leader in early 20thcentury India, known for promoting Hindu-Muslim harmony and unity within the Muslim community. A key figure in the Swadeshi movement, Hussain led processions of youths chanting "Vande Mataram," often placing himself at the forefront in defiance of the police was crucial in fostering national unity, patriotism, and political awareness in Undivided Bengal.

s: Who among the following Indian is known as Gurudev?
x: Rabindranath Tagore was an icon of Indian culture. He was a poet, philosopher, musician, writer, and educationist. He was popularly called as Gurudev. He also became the first Asian to become a Nobel laureate when he won Nobel Prize for 'Song Offerings', the English translation of his collection of poems, Gitanjali, in 1913 AD; he was awarded knighthood by the British King George V. He established Visva Bharati University in 1921 AD.

s: Who wrote the book, Desher Katha?
x: Desher Katha was written by Sakharam Ganesh, published in 1904. It is a document of the screams of the living Indian public in the chains of slavery and torture of exploitation in the British Empire. Sakharam Ganesh Deuskar, thinker of the Indian public awakening who had a wonderful confluence of localism and pan-Indianness in his thinking and writing. Born and raised in a Bengali environment but of Marathi origin, Deuskar acted as a bridge between the renaissance of Maharashtra and Bengal.

s: Who among the following were the critics of Swadeshi' movement and pleaded for a better understanding between the East and the West?
x: Rabindranath Tagore’s political acumen exhibited a marked ambivalence. On the one hand, he denounced European imperialism, occasionally voicing full support for Indian nationalist. On the other hand, he also shunned the Swadeshi movement, denouncing it in his acrid September, 1925 A.D. essay “The Cult of the Chakra” (an allusion to elements of Gandhism and the Non-cooperation Movement). In addition, he viewed British control of India as a “Political symptom of our social disease.” Urging Indians to accept blind revolution but of steady and purposeful education.

s: Who among the following established “Indian Society of Oriental Art”?
x: Abanindranath Tagore founded Indian Society of Oriental Art in Kolkata in 1907 to revive the ancient art traditions of India. He was the vice-principal of Government School of Art and a great artist of modern India.

s: Who among the following had founded the ‘Indian Society of Oriental Art’ to revive ancient art traditions of India?
x: First Indian artist to gain international recognition, Abanindranath Tagore (which was initiated by E.B. Havell) was the principal artist and founder of ‘Indian Society of Oriental Art’. His elder brother Gaganendranath Tagore was also artists. He was a major exponent of Swadeshi values in Indian art and inspired the new life in Indian School of Art. Congress: Benaras, Calcutta, and Surat Session *Gopal Krishna Gokhale chaired the 1905 A.D. Benaras session of Congress. He founded the 'Servants of India Society' the same year. In 1906, the Congress party was divided on the issue of the presidentship of the Calcutta session but the division was avoided when an agreement was reached on the name of Dadabhai Naoroji. Resolutions on Swaraj (selfgovernment), Swadeshi, Boycott and National education were passed in the Calcutta session in 1906 A.D. *Dadabhai Naoroji also remembered as 'Grand Old Man of India' was the first Indian who got elected to British Parliament in 1892 from central Finsbury constituency on a ticket of Liberal Party. He was the president of Congress in 1886, 1893 and 1906 sessions. He was the first Indian to be appointed as professor of Maths and Natural Philosophy at Elphinstone College, Mumbai. In 1851 A.D., he started Gujarati newspaper named as 'Rast Goftar'. *C.Y. Chintamani said that many intelligent and selfless leaders had embellished for the people of India, but in his era, no one was as the Dadabhai Naoroji. *Gokhale said, "If there is the divine in man

s: Vande Mataram became the theme song of the Indian National Movement during –
x: During Swadeshi Movement, the actual day of partition, October 16, 1905 A.D., was declared a day of mourning throughout Bengal and the hearths in the houses were kept unlit. People tied rakhis on each other wrists as a symbol of brotherhood. In Calcutta, most of the offices were kept closed, and a strike was observed in some jute mills and railway workshops. The streets reverberated with Vande Mataram which became the overnight National Song of Bengal and later, the Theme ralley cry or anthem of the National Movement.

s: The song ‘Amar Sonar Bangla’ written during the Swadeshi Movement of India inspired the liberation struggle of Bangladesh and was adopted as the National Anthem of Bangladesh. Who wrote this song?
x: The song ‘Amar Sonar Bangla’ was written and composed by Rabindranath Tagore during the Bengal partition movement of 1905. The music of this song is inspired by the melody of the Hymn ‘Ami Kothay Pabo Tare’ written by Gagan Harkara. Bangladesh adopted the first 10 lines of this song as its National Anthem. Syed Ali Ahsan translated the song into English. It is noteworthy that Rabindranath Tagore wrote the National Anthem of India ‘Jana Gana Mana’. He is the only poet in the world whose compositions have been adopted as the national anthem of the two countries.

x: Rabindranath Tagore did not favour the economic aspects of the Swadeshi Movement. He portrayed the side effects of the economic aspects of the Swadeshi Movement in his novel ‘Ghare Baire’ with depicting the sourness of Muslim businessmen. Remaining statements are correct.

s: Who among the following was one of the founders of the Indian Society of Oriental Art?
x: The Indian Society of Oriental Art (1907) was founded by Abanindranath and Gaganendranath Tagore, so Abanindranath Tagore is correct; Rabindranath was a different Tagore.

s: The first criminal case was registered during the Vande Mataram Movement in Andhra?
x:
The Kakinada Riot Case is regarded as the first criminal case registered in Andhra during the Vande Mataram Movement. The Vande Mataram Movement, inspired by the Swadeshi Movement following the Partition of Bengal (1905), spread nationalist ideas among students and the public. In Andhra, Kakinada emerged as one of the important centres of nationalist activity. The registration of the Kakinada Riot Case reflected the British Government's attempt to suppress the growing nationalist movement through legal action. Hence, the correct answer is Option (2).

• First Criminal Case during Vande Mataram Movement – Kakinada Riot Case
• Movement – Swadeshi / Vande Mataram Movement

The Young Men's Association played an important role in organizing the visit of Bipin Chandra Pal to Rajahmundry during the Swadeshi Movement. His speeches inspired students and young people to support the ideals of Swadeshi, National Education and Boycott of foreign goods. His visit significantly strengthened the nationalist movement in Andhra. Hence, the correct answer is Option (3).

• Leader Invited – Bipin Chandra Pal

s:
Arrange the following events in their chronological order and select the correct answer by using the codes given at the end:
1. Decision for partition of Bengal.
2. Acceptance of Swaraj as the goal of Congress.
3. Formal declaration of Swadeshi Movement.
4. Surat Split.
x: The partition of Bengal was declared on July 20, 1905. The official declaration of Swadeshi Movement was announced on August 7, 1905 at a conference held at Town Hall, Calcutta. Indian National Congress took a positive step in its Calcutta Session regarding the national movement. In his presidential speech, Dadabhai Naoroji said that the main aim of the Indian National Congress was to establish its own Government just like Britain and its dominion. It means the establishment of self-Government was adopted as the main aim of the Indian National Congress. In 1907, during Surat Session, there was split in the INC on the issue of Swadeshi.

s:
The following programmes were launched by the nationalist against the partition of Bengal :
1. Boycott
2. Swadeshi
3. Non-cooperation
4. National education
Select the correct answer :
x: The partition of Bengal in 1905 A.D. led to Swadeshi and Boycott Movement. Swadeshi Movement was complementary to ‘Boycott Movement.’ With the boycott of foreign goods, the use of ‘Swadeshi’ or indigenous goods increased. ‘Swadeshi’ was not altogether a noble idea. The movement spread to all classes and groups of people, including women and children, school and college students. This made the British to reverse the order of partition of Bengal. The boycott and Swadeshi Movements helped in the establishment of Swadeshi industries - textile mills, banks, chemical works and insurance companies. Swadeshi Stores were opened. National education and Indian languages were encouraged.

s: The Tenali Bomb Case happened during which movement?
x:
The Tenali Bomb Case occurred during the Vande Mataram Movement, which gained momentum after the Partition of Bengal (1905). Incident Details
• A bomb explosion occurred on a footpath between the villages of Nandivelugu and Tenali.
• A local man named Chennugadu died on the spot from the blast.
• The trial court convicted a local resident named Chukkapalli Ramayya for the bombing and murder. It involved the application of early colonial explosives legislation, specifically the Explosive Substances Act of 1908 The movement encouraged boycott of foreign goods, promotion of Swadeshi and nationalist activities. Revolutionary incidents such as the Tenali Bomb Case reflected the growing militant phase of nationalism in Andhra. Hence, the correct answer is Option (1).
